rule.name: ConcatenationComparedWithNull
rule.message: A string concatenation is compared with null. A concatenation is never null, so == null is always false and != null is always true, and the value that was meant to be tested is never checked. + binds tighter than == and !=, so "id=" + name != null ? name.trim() : "none" reads ("id=" + name) != null ? ...; when a conditional follows, put the parentheses around it: "id=" + (name != null ? name.trim() : "none"). Otherwise compare the value itself with null, or drop the comparison.
